loanOptions.title: Loan Options
loanOptions.description: Explore mortgage programs available in Florida.
loanOptions.heading: Loan Options
loanOptions.helper: Every program here is available across Florida. Compare them below, or tell me your situation and I'll point you to the right one.

fha.title: FHA Loans
fha.description: Flexible requirements for FHA loans in Florida.
fha.heading: FHA Loans
fha.heroTitle: A smaller down payment doesn't have to stop you
fha.heroSub: If your savings are limited or your credit history isn't perfect, an FHA loan keeps the door open.
fha.blurb: Flexible credit requirements and a down payment as low as 3.5%. Often the first step into homeownership.
fha.intro: An FHA loan is insured by the federal government, which is why lenders can approve buyers that conventional programs sometimes turn away. It's built for people who are still building credit or savings, not for those who already have both figured out. I use it often with first-time buyers.

whatIs.title: What is an FHA loan?
whatIs.body: An FHA loan is a mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration, a federal agency, so the lender takes on less risk than with a conventional loan. That backing is what lets you qualify with a down payment from 3.5% and a credit score that a conventional program might not accept. In exchange, you'll pay mortgage insurance for part or all of the loan term, unlike a conventional loan where it can usually be removed once you build enough equity.

required.title: What do you need for an FHA loan?
required.body: You'll need proof of income, two years of work history, and a credit score that meets the program minimum — flexible, but not without requirements. The home has to be your primary residence, not a rental or vacation property. A past bankruptcy or foreclosure doesn't automatically disqualify you, but there's a waiting period I'll confirm with you case by case. I'll tell you which documents to gather before you start looking at homes.

how.title: How an FHA loan works
items: Down payments starting at 3.5% of the purchase price.
Fixed terms commonly available in 15 or 30 years.
Mortgage insurance included in your monthly payment, for part or all of the loan.
No penalty for paying off the loan early.

conventional.title: Conventional Loans
conventional.heading: Conventional Loans
conventional.heroTitle: Solid credit opens the door to better terms
conventional.heroSub: If your credit and income are already strong, a conventional loan usually costs you less over time.
conventional.blurb: Competitive rates and terms if your credit is solid. Down payments starting around 3%.
conventional.intro: A conventional loan is the standard mortgage — not backed by a government agency, and usually the better deal once your credit and savings are established. It rewards a stronger financial profile with lower long-term costs. I compare it against FHA for almost every buyer who qualifies for both.

whatIs.title: What is a conventional loan?
whatIs.body: A conventional loan is a mortgage that isn't insured or guaranteed by a government agency, which means the lender relies more heavily on your credit and income. With solid credit, it typically comes with a down payment starting around 3%, competitive rates, and terms that can be more flexible than FHA. Unlike FHA, the mortgage insurance on a conventional loan can usually be removed once you reach a set level of equity — often around 20%.

required.title: What do you need for a conventional loan?
required.body: Lenders generally look for a stronger credit score than FHA requires, along with steady income and two years of employment history. Down payments start around 3%, though a larger down payment can lower your rate and remove mortgage insurance sooner. You can use it for a primary residence, a second home, or an investment property, which FHA doesn't allow. I'll walk through your credit report with you before we apply, so there are no surprises.

how.title: How a conventional loan works
items: Down payments starting around 3%, higher for second homes or investment properties.
Fixed terms commonly available in 15, 20, or 30 years.
Mortgage insurance that can be removed once you build enough equity.
No penalty for paying off the loan early.

va.title: VA Loans
va.description: VA loan benefits for veterans and service members.
va.heading: VA Loans
va.heroTitle: Buy with $0 down, backed by your service
va.heroSub: If you served, your benefit can cover the down payment most other buyers have to save for.
va.blurb: A benefit earned through service — often no down payment and no monthly mortgage insurance.
va.intro: A VA loan is a benefit for eligible veterans, active-duty service members, and some surviving spouses, guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs. It's one of the few programs that can finance a home with no down payment at all. I confirm your eligibility first, before we talk about anything else.

whatIs.title: What is a VA loan?
whatIs.body: A VA loan is a mortgage guaranteed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs for eligible veterans, active-duty service members, and certain surviving spouses. The guarantee is what allows lenders to offer it with no down payment and no monthly mortgage insurance, which sets it apart from both FHA and conventional loans. You'll pay a one-time funding fee in most cases, though some borrowers are exempt.

required.title: What do you need for a VA loan?
required.body: You'll need a Certificate of Eligibility, which confirms your service meets the program's requirements — I can help you request it if you don't already have one. There's no minimum down payment and no fixed minimum credit score from the VA itself, though lenders apply their own guidelines. The home must be your primary residence. Credit flexibility is real, but your income and debt still have to support the payment.

how.title: How a VA loan works
items: No down payment required in most cases.
No monthly mortgage insurance.
Fixed terms commonly available in 15 or 30 years.
A one-time funding fee, waived for some borrowers with a service-connected disability.

firstTimeHomebuyer.title: First Time Homebuyer
firstTimeHomebuyer.description: Programs for first time homebuyers in Florida.
firstTimeHomebuyer.heading: First Time Homebuyer
firstTimeHomebuyer.heroTitle: Florida help for your first down payment
firstTimeHomebuyer.heroSub: If saving for a down payment feels like the hardest part, Florida assistance programs may cover more of it than you think.
firstTimeHomebuyer.blurb: Down payment and closing cost assistance for first-time buyers in Florida, paired with FHA or conventional financing.
firstTimeHomebuyer.intro: First-time buyer programs aren't a separate loan — they're assistance layered on top of an FHA or conventional mortgage to help with the down payment and closing costs. Florida offers several of these, and most buyers never ask about them. I check what you qualify for before you start house hunting, not after.

whatIs.title: What is first-time homebuyer assistance?
whatIs.body: First-time homebuyer assistance combines a standard mortgage — usually FHA or conventional — with a Florida program that helps cover your down payment or closing costs, sometimes as a grant and sometimes as a low-interest second loan. It's not a different type of mortgage; it's help layered on top of one you'd already qualify for. The programs available and how much they cover change depending on income, location, and purchase price.

required.title: What do you need for first-time buyer assistance?
required.body: You'll generally need to be purchasing your first home — or your first home in several years, depending on the program — and your household income has to fall within the program's limits. You'll still go through the same credit and income approval as any FHA or conventional loan. Some programs require a short homebuyer education course, which I'll point you to if it applies. I'll tell you upfront which programs you're likely to qualify for.

how.title: How first-time buyer assistance works
items: Paired with an FHA or conventional loan, not a standalone mortgage.
Covers part of your down payment or closing costs, as a grant or a second loan.
Income limits that vary by county and household size.
Some programs require a short homebuyer education course.

refinance.title: Refinance
refinance.heading: Refinance
refinance.heroTitle: Lower your payment, or put your equity to work
refinance.heroSub: If your rate, your term, or your monthly payment no longer fits, refinancing might be worth a look.
refinance.blurb: Lower your rate, shorten your term, remove mortgage insurance, or take cash out from your equity.
refinance.intro: Refinancing replaces your current mortgage with a new one, on new terms. Sometimes it's about a lower monthly payment, sometimes about paying off the home faster, and sometimes about pulling out equity you've already built. It only makes sense in some cases — I'll tell you honestly when it doesn't.

whatIs.title: What is a refinance?
whatIs.body: Refinancing means paying off your current mortgage with a new loan, ideally on better terms. That can mean a lower interest rate, a shorter or longer term, the removal of mortgage insurance once you have enough equity, or a cash-out refinance that lets you borrow against the value you've built. The right move depends on your current rate, how long you plan to stay, and what you're trying to solve.

required.title: What do you need to refinance?
required.body: You'll need enough equity in your home — the exact amount depends on the type of refinance — along with income and credit that support the new loan. A cash-out refinance usually requires more equity than a rate-and-term refinance. Closing costs apply, similar to a purchase, so I run the numbers to see how long it takes to break even. If the math doesn't work in your favor, I'll say so.

how.title: How a refinance works
items: Replaces your current mortgage with a new rate, term, or loan amount.
Cash-out option lets you borrow against your home's equity.
Closing costs apply, similar to a home purchase.
A break-even point tells you how long it takes to come out ahead.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How we handle your personal information.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy

sections.title: What information we collect
sections.body: When you reach out — through the contact page, WhatsApp, a phone call, or (once it's live) the loan questionnaire — I collect what you give me: your name, phone number, email, and anything you share about your income, credit, or the property you're looking at. I don't collect anything else about you behind the scenes.

sections.title: How we use it
sections.body: Your information is used to answer your questions, prepare a loan quote, and follow up with you about your mortgage. It isn't used for anything beyond that — no unrelated marketing, no resale.

sections.title: Who we share it with
sections.body: Your information stays between you and me, except where it's genuinely needed to move your loan forward — for example, with a lender during the application process. Any customer relationship or email tools we add in a later phase will be documented here before they're used.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask what information I have on file for you, ask me to correct it, or ask me to delete it. Contact me directly and I'll take care of it personally.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: This site doesn't use analytics or tracking cookies today. If that changes, this page will say so before it happens.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.description: Our commitment to an accessible website.
accessibility.heading: Accessibility Statement

sections.title: Our commitment
sections.body: This site is built to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA, the standard most commonly used to judge whether a website works for people with disabilities. It's a goal I take seriously, not a checkbox — a mortgage is confusing enough without an inaccessible website in the way.

sections.title: What we've built in
sections.body: Color combinations are checked for contrast, every interactive element works from a keyboard alone, focus is always visible so you can see where you are, and the page structure uses proper HTML headings and landmarks so screen readers can make sense of it.

sections.title: Found a barrier?
sections.body: If any part of this site is hard to use with a screen reader, keyboard, or other assistive technology, tell me directly — the phone, email, and WhatsApp on the contact page all reach me personally — and I'll fix it or find another way to get you the same information.

sections.title: An ongoing effort
sections.body: Accessibility isn't a one-time fix. As this site grows, I'll keep testing it and correcting what falls short.
